test_title: PYST 33: RRB Group D - GS (Held On: 11 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct?

options.text: The value of G is constant everywhere
Gravitational force is strongest among small bodies
Every object attracts every other object in the universe

solution:
The correct answer is __**Gravitational force is strongest among small bodies**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The value of G is constant everywhere:**

 
 
• The gravitational constant (G) is a universal constant with a value of approximately **6.674 × 10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg²**. It remains constant throughout the universe.
 
• This constant is fundamental to Newton's law of gravitation, which governs the attractive force between two masses. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
 
 
• **Gravitational force is always attractive:**
 
 
• Gravitational force acts as an attractive force between two masses, pulling them towards each other.
 
• Unlike other forces such as electromagnetic forces, gravity does not have a repulsive component. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
 
 
• **Gravitational force is strongest among small bodies:**
 
 
• This statement is incorrect as gravitational force depends on the **masses** of the objects and the **distance** between them.
 
• Gravitational force is **stronger between large celestial bodies**, such as planets, stars, or moons, compared to smaller objects due to their larger masses.
 
• For small objects, the gravitational force is negligible. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*
 
 
 
• **Every object attracts every other object in the universe:**
 
 
• According to Newton's Universal Law of Gravitation, **every object in the universe exerts a gravitational pull** on every other object.
 
• This mutual attraction is proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centers. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Newton's Universal Law of Gravitation:**

 
 
• The law states that **every mass in the universe attracts every other mass** with a force that is directly proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centers.
 
• The formula is given by: **F = G × (m₁ × m₂) / r²**, where F is the gravitational force, m₁ and m₂ are the masses of the two objects, r is the distance between their centers, and G is the gravitational constant.
 
 
 
• **Gravitational Force Characteristics:**
 
 
• It is a **long-range force** that acts over astronomical distances.
 
• It is the **weakest of the fundamental forces** but dominates at large scales due to its cumulative effect over massive bodies.
 
• It is always **attractive** and never repulsive.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Gravity:**
 
 
• Gravity is responsible for holding planets in orbit around the sun and moons in orbit around planets.
 
• It governs the motion of celestial bodies, ocean tides, and the structure of galaxies.
 
• It plays a crucial role in phenomena such as free fall and weight measurement.
 
 
 
• **Role of Mass and Distance:**
 
 
• Greater the mass of the objects, stronger is the gravitational force.
 
• Greater the distance between the objects, weaker is the gravitational force due to the inverse square law.
 
 
 
• **Gravity on Different Celestial Bodies:**
 
 
• The acceleration due to gravity varies on different celestial bodies due to differences in their mass and radius.
 
• For example, the gravity on the Moon is about **1/6th** of Earth's gravity, making objects weigh less on the Moon.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Gravitational Constant:**

 
 
• Its value is **6.674 × 10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg²**.
 
• G is a universal constant and remains the same irrespective of location.
 
 
 
• **Inverse Square Law:**
 
 
• The gravitational force decreases as the square of the distance between two objects increases.
 
• This is why celestial bodies far apart exert negligible gravitational force on each other.
 
 
 
• **Gravitational Force vs. Other Forces:**
 
 
• Gravity is weaker compared to electromagnetic and nuclear forces but dominates over large distances.
 
• It plays a fundamental role in shaping the universe's structure.
 
 
 
• **Weight vs. Mass:**
 
 
• Mass is a measure of the amount of matter in an object and remains constant everywhere.
 
• Weight is the gravitational force acting on an object and depends on the location due to variations in gravity.
